questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Every time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If hazardous materials in the truck weigh more than 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials can be inhaled.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of materials are being carried and warn others of the dangers.

questions.question: What happens when you drive down a hill?

options.text: Your speed stays the same.
Your speed decreases.
Your speed increases.
You slow to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed increases.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle faster when you drive downhill, so your speed will increase.

questions.question: If you don't know how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?

options.text: Use water.
Stay in the vehicle.
Wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for firefighters to arrive.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters. Let them handle the fire safely.

questions.question: When you pull over to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.
Turn on the emergency flashers.
Wave your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What is the horn used for?

options.text: To show that you are angry at other drivers.
To warn other drivers that you are nearby.
To frighten other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers that you are nearby.
questions.explanation: Your horn warns others of your presence. Only use it when necessary because it can startle other drivers and create danger.

questions.question: What should happen if a bus breaks down while passengers are still aboard?

options.text: Another bus should push it to the destination.
The bus should be towed to the destination.
Passengers should push the bus.
The bus should be towed to the nearest safe place so passengers can exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus should be towed to the nearest safe place so passengers can exit.
questions.explanation: A broken-down bus with passengers should not be towed or pushed unless absolutely necessary. If towing is needed, only tow it to the nearest safe location where passengers can safely get off.

questions.question: If you have an intoxicated passenger on your bus, what should you do?

options.text: Make them exit the bus immediately.
Wait until you reach a safe area, like a scheduled stop or well-lit location, to have them exit.
Give them coffee to help them sober up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you reach a safe area, like a scheduled stop or well-lit location, to have them exit.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for your passenger's safety, even if they are intoxicated. Have them exit at a safe place, such as the next scheduled stop or another well-lit area with people nearby.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum following distance?

options.text: Four seconds.
Five seconds.
Six seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Six seconds.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one extra second.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: 10 feet of your vehicle.
1,000 feet of your vehicle.
The distance you can see ahead on the road.
One minute after you press the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: You must always be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. When visibility is low, slow down so you can stop safely.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?

options.text: Extra electrical fuses.
A loud horn.
A battery-operated flashlight.
Fireworks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extra electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles (such as reflective triangles).

questions.question: When making tight turns or maneuvers, a driver should:

options.text: Open the door for a better view.
Check their mirrors.
Flash their headlights.
Open their cargo door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check their mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors while driving. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Open the radiator cap quickly.
Not wear gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool down before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool down before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Wear gloves or use a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release the pressure.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no more than three feet high.
Must be secured to prevent it from moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be secured to prevent it from moving.
questions.explanation: All cargo in a trailer must be properly secured so it does not shift during transport.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.
Freeze before other road surfaces.
Have heaters to prevent freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular roads. Be extra careful when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The trailer is straight.
There is no trailer attached.
The vehicle is on a slight uphill slope.
The vehicle is on a slight downhill slope.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a truck, you can only check mirror adjustment correctly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: If a person tries to board a bus with a gasoline container, the driver should:

options.text: Place the container near the back of the bus.
Place the container near the front of the bus.
Place the container in the aisle.
Not allow the container on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allow the container on the bus.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must not allow hazardous materials like gasoline or car batteries onto the bus.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Say nothing and hope the problem goes away.
Write a report describing your concerns.
Try to fix the problem yourself.
Avoid using that part and hope no one notices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each driving day, write a report about any vehicles you drove. Note any safety issues or problems that could cause a breakdown.

questions.question: In cold weather, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces in cold weather. Use extra caution on bridges and overpasses during cold, wet weather.

questions.question: Mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only when changing lanes.
Checked often.
Checked only if you suspect a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving to watch traffic and check for problems on your vehicle.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck, you should:

options.text: Change gears while driving uphill.
Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.
